rationale:
Evidence: the best measured design is iteration 8 (dev score 50.39). It uses five sensors at y = 0.06 m, x = -0.03 to +0.03 m, a 0.016 m footprint, mass 0.8 kg, wheel_track 0.12 m, base_speed 1.4, kp 2.0, ki 1.0, kd 0.1, linear weights and search_right. Every 2026 development trial to date has ended off track after one line-loss event, with oval progress near 0.115 and s-bend progress near 0.1475.

What I kept from the round-1 critique: the draft (entity0) changes four or more variables at once (mass, wheel_track, base_speed, kd, sensor layout and array size). None of these changes has evidence behind it, and the critique is right that the mass and track changes pull the turn response in opposite directions. The draft's base_speed 0.9 and kd 0.8 are also untested, and kd 0.8 has an unresolved saturation risk. I also accept that the draft's 7-sensor, y = 0.08 layout does not match the best measured design.

What I rejected: I did not accept the critique's claim that kd is always harmful. Iteration 6 showed that dropping kd from 0.1 to 0.05 cut s-bend progress from 0.148 to 0.040, so kd has a real effect. I also did not take the critique's suggestion to test start handling in this race. This is the final iteration, and the unseen-track score depends on the robustness of a measured design, not on a new diagnostic.

Change: none. I resubmit the iteration 8 design unchanged. It is the only candidate with a measured score above 50 on the development tracks, and every alternative I considered adds untested changes. Expected result: a dev score close to 50.4, with the failure at the same first line loss. Completion is unlikely within 3 s.
